key_insight: An AI-assisted pipeline evaluates research-level mathematical proofs across multiple formats, reducing false-positive judgments compared with one-shot LLM evaluation.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a methodology for scaling semantic and logical verification of mathematical reasoning and supporting computational artifacts.
method: Analyze Ramanujan Challenge submissions involving research-level number theory.
Assess natural language proofs, computer algebra code, and Lean formalizations for semantic and logical correctness.
Compare pipeline judgments with conventional one-shot LLM evaluation.
evidence_signal: The pipeline reduced false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and increased supporting-code judgment accuracy from 46% to 58%.
watch_item: Residual evaluation errors remain, and generalization beyond the Challenge’s number-theory submissions is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
